title: How to Cook 90% of Chinese Food With 5 Foolproof Formulas
creator: Lilly Song
whenToUse: Pick a category formula instead of a memorized recipe when improvising Chinese household staples.
justinNotes: mild (oyster sauce OK, no chili); HP meat versions; LC veg-forward swaps
formula: Learn category formulas, not individual recipes — then cook almost anything without a recipe.
summary: Learn category formulas, not individual recipes — then cook almost anything without a recipe.
chefNotes: When Justin asks to cook Chinese-ish from fridge ingredients (or “make me something”), classify the main components into one of the five formulas, open that card, apply Justin adaptations, and write a Recommendation — do not dump into viral library unless asked to save.
Gaps: Velveting, stir-fry sauce ratios, Shaoxing / soy / sesame specifics, marinade formulas, wok oil-temp cues. Creator teases follow-up videos; add cards when those land.

formulas.formula: Thin veg → high heat + garlic + salt
Dense veg → blanch → medium + garlic, salt, oyster sauce
Meat → marinate → sear high → hold → aromatics/veg low → meat back → season
Eggs → slant-beat → high cook → remove → cook veg → fold eggs back
Braise → blanch meat → render fat → aromatics → season → simmer → high reduce

frameworks: Category > recipe — match the ingredient to a formula family, then improvise.
Heat matching density — thin → high; dense → blanch then medium; meat sear → high; aromatics/veg after meat → low; braise finish → high reduce.
Cook-apart, recombine — meat and eggs cooked separately from veg, then returned (protects texture).
Blanch when needed — dense veg (doneness) and braise meat (impurities).
Build then concentrate — braise: simmer covered for flavor, then reduce for glaze.

title: Thin vegetable stir-fry (garlic + salt)
creator: Lilly Song
whenToUse: Leafy or quick-cook thin vegetables that don’t need blanching.
justinNotes: mild — garlic + salt only (no chili); HP — add pre-cooked chicken/shrimp at end; LC — veg-forward, skip noodles/rice or use cauliflower rice
formula: Thin veg → high heat + garlic + salt → done.
summary: Leafy or quick-cook thin vegetables that don’t need blanching.
exampleIngredients: Bok choy leaves, spinach, bean sprouts, thinly sliced peppers, napa cabbage leaves, pea shoots
Oil: not specified in source (neutral high-smoke oil is fine)
chefNotes: Justin has thin leafy veg (or “something green quick”) → apply this card.
Keep seasoning minimal: garlic + salt; oyster sauce belongs on the **dense** card.
For a full meal: pair with a protein via [meat-stir-fry](meat-stir-fry.md) or fold eggs via [egg-dishes](egg-dishes.md), or suggest as a side.

justinAdaptations.how: Garlic + salt only; no chili oil, no white pepper heat, no spicy bean paste
Finish with sliced cooked chicken breast, shrimp, or firm tofu; or cook meat first with meat-stir-fry card then add thin veg last on high
Veg as the main volume; skip rice/noodles or serve over cauliflower rice / shirataki

title: Dense vegetable stir-fry (blanch → oyster sauce)
creator: Lilly Song
whenToUse: Thick or denser vegetables that need blanching before stir-fry for even doneness.
justinNotes: mild — oyster sauce OK, no chili; HP — add meat after veg or use meat-stir-fry pattern; LC — veg-forward plate, light oyster sauce
formula: Dense veg → blanch → medium stir-fry with garlic, salt, oyster sauce.
summary: Thick or denser vegetables that need blanching before stir-fry for even doneness.
exampleIngredients: Broccoli, cauliflower, thick bok choy stems, carrots, green beans, asparagus, gai lan stems
Named seasonings: garlic, salt, oyster sauce (only named finishing sauce in the veg formulas)
chefNotes: Fridge has broccoli / thick stems / denser veg → this card, not thin-veg.
Blanch briefly for doneness, drain well, then medium stir-fry with garlic, salt, oyster sauce.
For HP: combine with [meat-stir-fry](meat-stir-fry.md) (sear meat first, hold, then dense veg on medium, recombine).

justinAdaptations.how: Oyster sauce OK; no chili, no spicy fermented pastes
Add chicken, beef, shrimp, or tofu; prefer meat-stir-fry order so protein stays tender
Keep veg volume high; use oyster sauce lightly (sugar content); skip starch sides or use cauliflower rice

title: Meat stir-fry (sear → hold → recombine)
creator: Lilly Song
whenToUse: Any protein + veg stir-fry where meat texture matters (chicken, beef, pork, shrimp).
justinNotes: mild — no chili in marinade/seasoning; HP — lean cuts, generous meat portion; LC — extra veg, light sauce, skip noodle base unless requested
formula: Marinate → sear meat high → hold → aromatics + veg low → meat back → season.
summary: Any protein + veg stir-fry where meat texture matters (chicken, beef, pork, shrimp).
exampleIngredients: Proteins: chicken thigh/breast, beef strips, pork, shrimp
Veg: match thin or dense cards (blanch dense veg first if needed)
Named elements in source: marinade (composition not given), aromatics (typically ginger/garlic/scallion — not named here), end seasoning (unspecified)
**Gaps in this Short:** velveting, cornstarch, baking soda, Shaoxing, soy ratios, slurry — improvise lightly or wait for follow-up cards
chefNotes: “Make me a stir-fry with [protein] and [veg]” → this card as the spine.
Choose veg path: [thin-veg](thin-veg-stir-fry.md) or [dense-veg](dense-veg-stir-fry.md) for the veg phase.
Keep mild: no chili; oyster sauce OK when finishing denser veg or as part of end seasoning.
Emit into **Recommendations**, not viral library, unless Justin wants it saved.

justinAdaptations.how: Marinade/seasoning without chili, chili oil, or spicy bean paste; oyster sauce + garlic/ginger OK
Lean chicken breast or beef; larger meat:veg ratio; optional egg white in marinade later if velveting card exists
Load veg; skip sugar-heavy sauces; serve without noodles/rice or with cauliflower rice

title: Egg dishes (slant-beat → fold)
creator: Lilly Song
whenToUse: Egg + vegetable dishes (tomato-egg, scrambled egg with greens, etc.).
justinNotes: mild — salt/garlic/scallion OK, no chili; HP — extra eggs or add chicken; LC — veg-heavy fold-ins, skip sweet tomato sauce sugar bombs or use stevia if sweetened
formula: Slant-beat eggs → high-heat cook → remove → cook veg → fold eggs back.
summary: Egg + vegetable dishes (tomato-egg, scrambled egg with greens, etc.).
steps: 1. Beat eggs **on a slant** to fluff
exampleIngredients: Eggs (fluffed by beating on a slant to incorporate air)
Veg: tomato, greens, chives/scallion, mushrooms, leftover thin/dense veg
Seasoning: not detailed in source — salt; garlic/scallion as aromatics if desired
chefNotes: Fridge has eggs + veg, or Justin wants a quick egg dish → this card.
Same “cook-apart → recombine” idea as [meat-stir-fry](meat-stir-fry.md) — protects egg texture.
Pair thin vs dense veg handling from the veg cards when veg needs blanching first.

justinAdaptations.how: No chili; keep classic savory (salt, garlic, scallion); oyster sauce sparingly if umami boost needed
More eggs; or add diced cooked chicken / shrimp when folding; egg + meat combo ok
Veg-forward fold-ins; if tomato-egg, skip sugar or use Justin sweetener swaps; no rice unless requested

title: Braised dishes (blanch → render → simmer → reduce)
creator: Lilly Song
whenToUse: Long-simmer braises (hong shao–style, soy-braised meats, etc.) when time allows.
justinNotes: mild — aromatics without chili/star-anise heat spikes; HP — meat-forward cuts; LC — reduce sugar in braise liquid, serve with veg not rice
formula: Blanch meat → render fat → aromatics → season → cover-simmer → high-heat reduce.
summary: Long-simmer braises (hong shao–style, soy-braised meats, etc.) when time allows.
steps: 2. Render the fat — Build base / flavor
6. Crank heat at end — Reduce sauce
exampleIngredients: Meats that benefit from braise: pork belly/shoulder, chicken legs/thighs, beef chunks
Aromatics: not listed in source (typically ginger, scallion, garlic)
Seasoning / liquid: not specified (soy, rock sugar, star anise, etc. are common but **not taught in this Short**)
chefNotes: Justin wants something cozy / make-ahead / “braised” → this skeleton.
Always blanch meat first (impurities), then render → aromatics → season → covered simmer → high reduce for glaze.
Fill liquid/seasoning gaps with mild Justin-safe defaults (light soy, a little oyster sauce, ginger/garlic/scallion; no chili). Note sugar → stevia/monk fruit if sweetening.
Gaps to acknowledge: master stock, specific spices, times — improvise conservatively.

justinAdaptations.how: No chili; go easy on aggressive spice; oyster sauce OK; ginger/garlic/scallion aromatics
Choose meaty cuts with good protein yield (chicken thighs, leaner pork/beef chunks); skim excess fat after render if desired
Minimize rock sugar / sweet braise liquids (use Justin sweeteners if needed); serve with greens or cauliflower rice instead of white rice
